change.before: the whole query was used as one substring, so “quiet temples weekend” returned nothing while the exact phrase worked
change.after: queries with two or more meaningful words are split (stopwords removed, max five) and matched across title, city and summary; single-word behaviour and destination aliases are unchanged
change.security: the PostgREST or-filter builder still quotes/escapes values and cannot touch published status; the security test now asserts the sanitized clause shape and that no “eq.” syntax leaks

local.api: quiet temples weekend → A quiet-temples weekend in Kyoto; single word and city filters unchanged
local.browser: the explore page rendered the Kyoto guide for the multi-word query
local.unit: full suite 2037 pass / 2 skip, including the updated catalogue security test

family trip singapore: Bali family resorts that actually work with young kids
Singapore with kids: the stroller-friendly route
quiet temples weekend: Chiang Mai on a backpacker budget

honestLimits: Matching is any-meaningful-word across title/city/summary; it improves recall but is not relevance-scored, so a generic word can pull in unrelated guides.
Search is still substring-based (no stemming, synonyms or typos); “family-friendly” and “family friendly” differ.
No database change: the mcp_search_guides RPC used by the studio assistant was not altered, so its tool queries keep their existing semantics.
